bears.name: Chicago Bears
bears.summary: Big day at Halas Hall, Bears fans. Chicago shipped defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. to Atlanta, bringing back cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round pick in a move that reshapes the interior D-line and adds secondary depth right before the opener. On the health front, Luther Burden sat out Saturday's preseason finale against Tennessee with a groin issue but did run routes pregame, while running back Booker's groin injury has him listed week-to-week as the roster settles into final form ahead of the Week 1 trip to Carolina.

lions.name: Detroit Lions
lions.summary: Good morning, Lions fans. Detroit is trimming down its 53-man roster after finishing the preseason, with cuts including familiar names like TE Tyler Conklin, LB Joe Bachie, and RB Trayveon Williams, while the team also added 14 players to its initial practice squad. On the injury front, safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch remain on the PUP list as they work back from injury and will have to miss the start of the regular season, and there's some concern around TE  Sam LaPorta, who is dealing with a hip injury, with Dan Campbell unwilling to guarantee he'll be ready for the September 13 opener.  On a brighter note, the Lions locked up a couple of core pieces long-term, announcing extensions for RB Jahmyr Gibbs and LB Jack Campbell through the 2030 season, so plenty to digest as the roster takes shape for Week 1.

packers.name: Green Bay Packers
packers.summary: Big shakeup in Green Bay today as the Packers finalized their 53-man roster, and general manager Brian Gutekunst stayed plenty busy doing it. The headline move sees  running back Josh Jacobs placed on the Commissioner's Exempt list pending an investigation into alleged domestic violence charges , which opened the door for the Packers to go get some backfield help —  Green Bay made a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers to acquire running back Kaleb Johnson . vikings.name: Minnesota Vikings
vikings.summary: Big couple of days in Eagan: the Vikings finalized their 53-man roster and kept all four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer — though it remains to be seen who ends up as Murray's backup by kickoff on Sept. 13.  The Vikings kept Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer at quarterback, and it's also up in the air whether McCarthy or Wentz will be Murray's backup.  Things stayed chaotic even after cuts, as  second-year QB Max Brosmer and rookie WR Dillon Bell became the first casualties from the initial 53-man roster just days after it was set , and Minnesota also shipped out young tackle Walter Rouse in a trade with New England. On the injury front, keep an eye on the edge rush depth —  the Vikings need an edge rusher after Tyler Batty tore his ACL in the preseason finale against Denver  — so don't be surprised if GM Nolan Teasley adds another veteran body before Week 1 against Green Bay.
